_comment: The one strict base every project's tsconfig extends: the five packages, apps/edge, apps/dashboard, and
apps/mobile beside Expo's own base. A project states only what its runtime needs on top (the edge's NodeNext
resolution, the dashboard's JSX and Next plugin, the phone app's React Native), never a strictness flag of its
own, so a flag added here reaches every project at once. tests/types/every-tsconfig-extends-the-base.test.mjs
On, beyond `strict`: noUncheckedIndexedAccess (an index read is T | undefined until checked; core, contracts and
the dashboard turn it off until their reads are guarded, and tests/types/index-reads-are-counted.test.mjs counts
each file's meanwhile, a number that may only fall), noImplicitOverride, noImplicitReturns,
noFallthroughCasesInSwitch, noUncheckedSideEffectImports, allowUnreachableCode false, verbatimModuleSyntax and
isolatedModules. The last two, with the lint's consistent-type-imports, make an import only a type reads say
`import type`, so every transpiler (tsup's esbuild, Next's SWC, Vercel's, Metro's Babel) drops what tsc drops.
Off on purpose: noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature (style only once index reads are checked; 1,669 findings),
exactOptionalPropertyTypes (JSON drops undefined, so the wire cannot tell absent from undefined; 208),
erasableSyntaxOnly (the tests run through tsx, not Node's type stripping) and isolatedDeclarations (the committed
dist/index.d.ts already shows every interface change in review).
